transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

A power cut and surge can easily blow the internal fuse on the appliance's main PCB, which would explain why there are no lights at all. Please plug a lamp or phone charger into that same socket to confirm it has power. If the socket works but the washer-dryer still shows nothing, the internal fuse on the PCB is likely blown, which requires an engineer to replace safely.

I tried a lamp in that socket and it works fine. The washer-dryer is still completely dead, even after leaving it unplugged for over 10 minutes. It might still be under an extended warranty too, but I'm not sure.

[Heading: Internal PCB fuse blown or main board failure]
Since the socket has power but your Candy washer-dryer remains completely dead (no lights or display), the most likely cause is that the internal fuse on the main control board blew during last night's power cut. This is a common result of electrical surges. Given your uncertainty about the warranty, I recommend contacting Candy support or your warranty provider first to see if this surge damage is covered before arranging a paid repair.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The label says CSOW 4965TWE/1-80, it's a Candy Smart Pro. Is there anything else I can check myself, or should I just contact Candy or the warranty company?

That model number confirms it's a Candy Smart Pro washer-dryer. Since the socket has power but the machine remains completely dead with no display or lights, this is almost certainly caused by the internal fuse on the main control board blowing during last night's surge. This is an internal electrical fault that cannot be safely fixed by replacing plugs or fuses at the wall; it requires a qualified engineer to open the unit and replace the PCB component.
